question: The original statue of this creature was sculpted by Lim Nang Seng and unveiled in 1972 by Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew. Alec Fraser-Brunner, the curator of the Van Kleef Aquarium, designed it in 1964 as a logo for the Singapore Tourist Promotion Board. The main statue stands 8.6 metres tall, weighs about 70 tonnes, and spouts water from its mouth. Its fish body represents Singapore's origins as a fishing village called Temasek. For 10 points, name this Singaporean mascot with the head of a lion and the body of a fish.
answer: Merlion

question: This resort was designed by the architect Moshe Safdie and developed by an American casino company. It opened in 2010 and includes a casino. Its three hotel towers are each about 55 storeys tall. They are topped by a platform 340 metres long that cantilevers out over one end, with a 150-metre infinity pool. For 10 points, name this Singapore hotel and casino resort whose rooftop SkyPark overlooks the city skyline.
answer: Marina Bay Sands [or MBS; prompt on "Marina Bay" or "Sands"]

question: This dish is believed to have evolved from a specialty of Wenchang, on an island in southern China. Immigrants from that island brought it to Southeast Asia in the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries. The bird is poached whole at a gentle heat, and the stock is kept. The grain is fried in the bird's fat, then cooked in that stock with ginger, garlic and pandan leaves. For 10 points, name this dish, served with chilli sauce, dark soy sauce and cucumber, that is called one of Singapore's national dishes.
answer: Hainanese chicken rice [prompt on "chicken" or "rice"; accept Hainanese chicken rice]

question: This island's former name has been translated as the island behind which lies death. Fort Siloso, one of several British forts built here in the late nineteenth century, guarded the harbour entrance. During the Second World War it held a prisoner-of-war camp. In 2018 the Capella hotel here hosted a summit between Donald Trump and Kim Jong Un. For 10 points, name this resort island off Singapore's southern coast that is home to Universal Studios Singapore and whose Malay name means peace and tranquillity.
answer: Sentosa [or Pulau Sentosa; do not accept "Blakang Mati"]

question: This man studied law at Cambridge and was called to the bar at the Middle Temple in 1950. He co-founded the People's Action Party in 1954 with colleagues including Goh Keng Swee and Toh Chin Chye. He became prime minister in 1959 at the age of 35 and held the office until 1990, then served as Senior Minister and Minister Mentor until 2011. He died on 23 March 2015, and one of his sons later also became prime minister. For 10 points, name this longtime prime minister of Singapore.
answer: Lee Kuan Yew [or LKY; prompt on "Lee"; do not accept or prompt on "Lee Hsien Loong"]

question: This man was born in 1781 aboard his father's ship off the coast of Jamaica. He served as Lieutenant-Governor of Java and later of Bencoolen, and wrote a two-volume history of Java. He was the first president of the Zoological Society of London. He is commemorated by a marble sculpture by Francis Chantrey in Westminster Abbey, though he is buried at Hendon. For 10 points, name this British official who landed on 29 January 1819 and founded a settlement on the island of Singapore.
answer: Sir Thomas Stamford Raffles [prompt on "Stamford"]

question: Linguists debate how much of this word comes from Malay, Hokkien and Cantonese, all of which have a similar sentence-final particle. It is one of the discourse particles of Colloquial Singapore English, alongside lor, leh, meh and hor. The Oxford English Dictionary added it in the year 2000. That was also the year the Speak Good English Movement was launched to discourage the variety of English in which it appears. For 10 points, give this one-syllable particle that ends many sentences in Singlish.
answer: lah [or la; prompt on "Singlish" or "particle"]

question: This athlete attended Anglo-Chinese School before enrolling at the University of Texas at Austin, where he was coached by Eddie Reese. At the 2015 SEA Games he broke a 33-year-old national record in the 50 metre freestyle. He received a S$1 million award from his government under its Multi-Million Dollar Award Programme. On 12 August 2016 he won the 100 metre butterfly in an Olympic record time, beating the mark set by Michael Phelps in 2008. For 10 points, name this swimmer who won his country's first Olympic gold medal in Rio de Janeiro.
answer: Joseph Schooling [prompt on "Joseph"]

question: The main road here was renamed from Reformatory Road in 1947 after a governor of the Straits Settlements, though historians disagree about which one. During the Japanese invasion of 1942, that road was one of the defence lines of the Malay Regiment in the Battle of Pasir Panjang. The Housing and Development Board built its eighth new town here between 1975 and 1979, partly on the site of Colombo Camp. Ngee Ann Polytechnic is located here, and its East-West Line station has the code EW23. For 10 points, name this town in western Singapore, between Jurong East and Dover on the MRT.
answer: Clementi [accept Clementi New Town]

question: The recipe for this cocktail was reportedly lost after the 1930s and reconstructed from a note written by a visitor in 1936. Its ingredients include gin, cherry liqueur, Benedictine, pineapple juice, lime juice, grenadine and Angostura bitters. It is traditionally credited to Ngiam Tong Boon, a bartender who created it in 1915 at the Long Bar of a famous colonial-era hotel. Its pink colour was meant to make it look like fruit juice, so that women could drink alcohol in public. For 10 points, name this gin-based cocktail, served in a hurricane glass and named for a Southeast Asian city-state.
answer: Singapore Sling [prompt on "sling" or "gin sling"]

question: A retaining wall collapsed on 20 April 2004 at a tunnel site near the Merdeka Bridge, killing four workers and delaying the opening of this line. Its Stage 3, from Bartley to Marymount, opened on 28 May 2009. It is the fourth line on its country's MRT network and is operated by SMRT Trains. It runs fully automated, three-car Alstom Metropolis trains controlled by the Urbalis signalling system. For 10 points, name this orange-coloured, driverless, orbital MRT line that links Singapore's radial lines.
answer: Circle Line [or CCL]

question: A causeway across the Johor Strait was blown up on 31 January to slow the advance that led to this event. Japanese troops crossed the strait on 8 February and attacked the weakly defended northwest of the island. On the morning of 15 February, Lieutenant-General Arthur Percival met eleven senior officers in the Battlebox, where they noted that less than 24 hours of water remained. That evening Percival signed an unconditional surrender to General Tomoyuki Yamashita in the boardroom of the Ford Factory. For 10 points, name this February 1942 surrender that Winston Churchill called the worst disaster and largest capitulation in British history and that began the Japanese occupation of Singapore.
answer: Fall of Singapore [or Battle of Singapore or Surrender of Singapore; prompt on "Singapore" or "Japanese occupation of Singapore"]

question: A file code-named Albatross, declassified in recent years, shows that this event was a negotiated decision rather than a sudden ejection. Finance Minister Goh Keng Swee proposed it to Tun Razak in July 1965. It followed communal riots in 1964 and the People's Action Party's decision to contest the federal election, in which it won just one seat. The federal Parliament approved it by a vote of 126 to 0, and Tunku Abdul Rahman announced it on 9 August 1965. For 10 points, name this event, two years after a merger, in which Singapore left Malaysia and became independent.
answer: separation of Singapore from Malaysia [or Singapore's expulsion from Malaysia or expulsion of Singapore from Malaysia; or independence of Singapore; accept word forms]

question: A 1990 parliamentary speech warned that ministers should not be infected by a "syndrome" of this word. It began as slang among conscripts doing National Service. It comes from a Hokkien expression whose Chinese characters mean afraid to lose. The Oxford English Dictionary added it in 2007 and made it a Word of the Day in 2015. For 10 points, give this Singlish adjective for a competitive fear of missing out, as in a parent who queues overnight for a school place.
answer: kiasu [or kiasuism or kiasuness; accept word forms; do not accept or prompt on "kiasi"]

question: Members of this community traditionally spoke a creole of Malay with Hokkien vocabulary that is now dying out. The women wore the kebaya and beaded slippers called kasut manik. Their cuisine blends Chinese ingredients with Malay spices, in dishes such as laksa and ayam buah keluak. Their origins are traced to Chinese traders who settled in Malacca and married local women. For 10 points, name this community of Chinese descendants in Malacca, Penang and Singapore, whose name comes from a Malay word for child.
answer: Peranakan [or Peranakan Chinese; or Straits Chinese; or Baba-Nyonya; or Baba and Nyonya]

question: A Chinese traveller named Wang Dayuan visited around 1330 and described two settlements here, Long Ya Men and Ban Zu. He recorded that a Siamese attack a few years earlier had failed to take the fortified city after a month. The Javanese poem Nagarakretagama, written in 1365, also mentions the place. The name likely derives from a Malay word for sea or lake. For 10 points, give this 14th-century name, meaning sea town, for the settlement on the site of modern Singapore, which was later replaced by Singapura and is now borne by a sovereign wealth fund.
answer: Temasek [or Tumasik or Tamasak or Danmaxi; prompt on "Singapura"; do not accept "Singapore"]

question: The composer of this piece was born in Bukittinggi in 1907 and wrote about 1,500 songs, including the song Semoga Bahagia. It was commissioned in 1958 by the City Council's deputy mayor, Ong Pang Boon, and first performed on 6 September 1958 at the reopening of the Victoria Theatre. In 2001 an official relaunch lowered its key from G major to F major. By law it may be sung only in Malay, though authorised translations exist in English, Mandarin and Tamil. For 10 points, name this piece by Zubir Said, Singapore's national anthem, whose title means Onward Singapore.
answer: Majulah Singapura [or Onward Singapore]

question: Colonel Masanobu Tsuji served as chief of planning for this operation, which General Tomoyuki Yamashita commanded. Its victims were killed at sites including Changi Beach, Punggol Point and Tanah Merah. The selection was arbitrary, and people were condemned for wearing glasses or having tattoos. Estimates of the toll vary widely, from under 5,000 in Japanese records to at least 50,000 in Singaporean ones. For 10 points, name this massacre of ethnic Chinese carried out from 18 February to 4 March 1942, whose Chinese name means purge through cleansing.
answer: Sook Ching [or Operation Sook Ching; or Sook Ching massacre; or Kakyo Shukusei; prompt on "Japanese occupation of Singapore"]

question: A judge named Algernon Brown declared a marriage void in December 1950, one solemnised when the bride was 13 to a 21-year-old man named Mansoor Adabi. The bride had been born in Tjimahi, Java, in 1937 and was given in 1943 to Che Aminah binte Mohamed, who raised her as a Muslim in Kemaman, Terengganu. After the judge awarded custody to her Dutch parents, photographs of the girl kneeling before a statue of the Virgin Mary inflamed Muslim opinion. The unrest lasted from 11 to 13 December, leaving 18 dead and 173 injured. For 10 points, name these 1950 riots in Singapore sparked by a custody battle over a Dutch-born girl.
answer: Maria Hertogh riots [or Natrah riots or Nadra riots; prompt on "Maria Hertogh" or "Natrah" or "Nadra"]

question: A Japanese-built fishing boat named Kofuku Maru was renamed after a small but deadly Asian snake for this operation. It sailed from Exmouth, Western Australia, on 1 September 1943. On the night of 26 September, six commandos in three folding canoes attached limpet mines to Japanese ships in Singapore Harbour. The Japanese blamed local saboteurs, leading to the Double Tenth incident of mass arrests, torture and executions. For 10 points, name this 1943 raid by Z Special Unit commandos led by Ivan Lyon, which was followed a year later by Operation Rimau.
answer: Operation Jaywick [prompt on "Krait" or "MV Krait"; do not accept "Operation Rimau"]
